name: Indo SMC Limited
summary: Hold — unresolved. sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Exact legal identity: INDO SMC LIMITED, ISIN INE 0 WKY 01013, BSE 544681 / INDOSMC, BSE SME; incorporated 27 September 2021, listed 21 January 2026. Current CIN L 71100 GJ 2021 PLC 125904 reflects later classification/public status, not a different issuer. Cutoff 20 October 2026; market observation 19 October, because 20 October is a market holiday. Research is standalone under Indian Accounting Standards AS/Companies Accounting Standards Rules 2021, not an IndAS consolidated model; no subsidiary/associate/JV reported in FY 26. Five-calendar-year boundary 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031, 15% nominal pretax equity hurdle. ₹5 lakh is illustrative: one 1000-share lot costs₹445800, two₹891600. Confidence is high that cited filings contain the reported amounts, medium for comparable growth, and low for incremental returns, current cash availability and trade execution. G1 Conditional; G2 Hold — unresolved; G3 Hold — unresolved; G4 Conditional. These are research gates, not allegations or default declarations.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Canonical factors: GOV 4, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 5, CAP NS, CASH 2, BAL NS, EXEC 5, EARN 5, R/D/P/L NS. BQS known contribution 3.66 at 80% coverage, mathematical missing-data bound 3.86–5.66; GQS known 5.15 at 85% coverage, raw missing-data bound 5.30–6.65. CASH 2 triggers the stated growth-quality cap 5, but the final GQS remainsNS rather than being replaced by 5. IAS has 0% coverage because Q requires the complete final BQS and all four investment factors remainNS; its 1–10 mathematical bound is uninformative. Exact Decimal weights and contributions accompany the record, without renormalization. GOV and EXEC are the two uncertain scored judgments: ±1 moves BQS known contribution by±0.20 or±0.08, combined±0.28. MOAT±1 adds±0.20; these sensitivities do not restore missing factors or clear gates. REV uses the predefined three-year schedule because no five-year full-period history exists: starting 9, no trajectory adjustment, Medium-confidence ceiling 8. Repeated cash weakness is not also used as an arbitrary penalty in every other factor.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The company manufactures sheet-moulding-compound enclosures and related products, FRP gratings/pultrusions and electrical current/potential-transformer products and cubicles. It earns through customer orders, production, dispatch/acceptance and credit collection, with technical approvals and tender competition affecting access. FY 26 SMC revenue₹63.97 cr, FRP₹23.75 cr and CTPT₹222.02 cr sum to the audited total within rounding; CTPT provides 71.68% of sales. Segment results are not standalone free cash flows or cohort returns. Ahmedabad, Nashik and Ghiloth feature in the business update. Q 1 FY 27 plant revenue₹21.46/64.68/1.99 cr sums₹88.13 cr versus rounded stated₹88.12 cr, not a new segment-accounting total. Revenue depends on a narrow customer base: H 1 FY 26 one unnamed customer contributes 65.12%, topfive 78.08%. Customer names are not inferred from marketing logos. The retrieved RHP indicates commercial repetition but no long-term guarantee that tender wins recur. FY 26 geographic revenue and current customer-level cash collection were not fully disclosed in the reviewed records.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: The plausible advantage is manufacturing know-how, electrical test/approval capability and relationships, rather than a proven patent, network or brand monopoly. RHP itself describes competitive tender allocation based on price, technical performance and delivery, so qualifications are an entry condition rather than proof of persistent excess pricing power. Repeat-customer counts improve, but one H 1 customer 65.12% and one supplier 61.32% weaken bargaining independence. Aeron Composite is useful FRP context: FY 25 presentation shows about₹215 cr revenue and 8.3% EBITDA margin. RMC Switchgears rating figures show₹318.16 cr consolidated revenue and 16.73% EBITDA margin with electrical/solar EPC exposure and working-capital constraints. Genus Power is a larger integrated metering/AMISP model, not a clean component peer. These distinct scopes make a mechanically averaged trading multiple inappropriate. MOAT 4 reflects material contestability despite real technical usefulness; demonstrable customer retention through pricing cycles, qualified alternate suppliers and sustained cash returns would be stronger evidence.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Four full annual observations run FY 23₹7.2955 cr, FY 24₹28.0338 cr, FY 25₹138.6925 cr and FY 26₹309.7393 cr. Absolute additions are₹20.7383 cr,₹110.6587 cr and₹171.0468 cr; three-year CAGR 248.8567%, average annual addition₹100.8146 cr. FY 22 revenue₹0.6914147 cr belongs to the short 27 September 2021–31 March 2022 startup period, so it is not a comparable five-year starting observation. No acquisition is identified, but a quantified price/volume/mix bridge is unavailable; gross revenue is not relabeled verified unit demand. FY 26 growth 123.32% and actual CTPT scale demonstrate rapid expansion. Q 1 FY 27 management revenue₹88.12 cr, up 135.96%, is a single operational update, not a TTM calculation or full-year run rate. H 1 FY 26 revenue₹112.5411 cr is a separately retained restated interim; no comparable prior interim cash-flow series supports synthetic TTM. May₹450–500 cr FY 27 targets and October₹31.71 cr orders are forward claims, not earned revenue.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The central distinction is installed capacity versus production versus attributable incremental cash return. FY 25 SMC output 2453.44 tonnes against year-end 4344 capacity equals 56.48%; FRP 838.28/1789 equals 46.86%. Late-year commissioning means those are not time-weighted utilization. Q 1 FY 27 SMC 229.18/6047 and FRP 636.02/3460 are output over annual installed capacity, not annualized utilization; quarterly mix and commissioning timing matter. HTCT 3000/12000, zeroLTCT and zero distribution-box output, and cubicles 360/1800 further show why heterogeneous capacity units cannot be summed into an earnings forecast. The updated monitor shows only₹1.2101 cr capex used byJune against₹25.7067 cr IPO allocation, with delayed purchasing and revised FY 27/FY 28 deployment. New approvals and orders create accessible options, not bankable projects. Accounting FY 26 ROIC≈32.53% and one-year NOPAT/IC-change proxy≈22.29% are diagnostic only: profit mix, restatement and working capital prevent attribution. CAP staysNS; no project IRR, cycle-tested unit economics or claim that IPO-funded capacity is already profitable.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: The positive execution evidence is the growth in audited operations and actual CTPT production. Against it, IPO capex scheduled for FY 26 was delayed, with management citing orders not placed, metal-price/geopolitical uncertainty and 3–4 month equipment lead times. CRISIL initially issued a May 15 issuer-non-cooperative monitoring report because requested documents were missing; the August 14 update followed later information. That information delivery is a resolution, not an enduring default rating, while capex delivery remains delayed. Neel Shah relinquished CFO duties 4 September citing limited time/attention but remained MD, and Anand Santosh Saraogi became CFO; this is not auditor resignation. FY 25 RPT sales₹17.4183 cr/purchases₹14.2355 cr and H 1 related receivables₹10.6288 cr warrant current detail, but ordinary-course/arm-length assertions are retained and no abusive transfer is established. Repeated lender-return and GST mismatches, incomplete FY 26 detailed RPT/ownership evidence and numerical inconsistencies justify GOV 4 and G1 Conditional rather than a fabricated fraud finding. Dates, original explanations and unresolved remediation requirements remain in the evidence ledger.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY 26 operating EBITDA₹46.8905 cr excludes₹0.756 cr other income; EBIT₹45.4510 cr, statutory PAT₹32.383 cr. Reported CFO−₹34.766 cr is explained by pre-working-capital cash₹46.1866 cr less inventory₹67.8469 cr, advances₹12.1731 cr, creditor/other movements and cash taxes, partly offset by₹11.3922 cr receivable release. Cash capex₹6.9178 cr belongs to investing cash flow and yields reported FCF proxy−₹41.6838 cr; it is not the explanation for negative CFO. Debt₹46.9498 cr and cash₹53.5547 cr do not prove net-cash resilience because₹49.44 cr is IPO earmarked and₹2.49 cr FD pledged, with overlap/spendability unresolved. Cash/current accounts are only₹1.0002 cr. Operating IC rises₹70.7243 cr to₹152.8179 cr and reconciles to financing within₹0.0001 cr rounding; it includes CWIP, capital advances and deposits, excludes cash/interest receivable, and separates financing/tax liabilities. One-year diagnostic ROIC cannot score CAP. Statutory versus IPO-restated FY 25 PAT₹16.8326/15.4409 cr and CFO−₹10.8958/−13.7034 cr remain parallel with documented tax/prior-period bridge; FD perimeter explains₹2.5184 cr of₹2.8076 cr CFO difference, residual₹0.2892 cr remains unverified. Unmodified opinion is positive, but unresolved GST, Q 3 bank-debtor gap₹22.9937 cr and annual narrative/EPS/material-cost inconsistencies prevent G2 clearance.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: Secondary price₹445.80 times 22,855,350 issued shares gives₹1,018.8915 cr equity value. FY 26 earnings on current shares are₹14.1687, so P/E 31.46×; using weighted dilutedEPS₹18.09 would show 24.64× and understate full post-IPO capitalization. An explicitly conservative cash perimeter gives EV/operatingEBITDA 22.71×; verified available-cash EV isND. Bear/base/bull models use FY 27 revenue₹340.71/450/500 cr, EBITDA margins 10.5/14.5/16%, later growth, annual working capital and capex, debt amortization, cash tax, legal-object IPO releases, and 8/12/16× terminal run-rate EBITDA. The exit metric is forecast full-FY 32 EBITDA used as an annual run-rate proxy at 19 October 2031, not trailing realized EBITDA or cash earnings; only cash flows through that October date enter equity value. Every non-rescue case begins below the analyst 2%revenue operating-cash floor, so even conditional non-rescue returns/entry prices are null. This is not proof of actual default. Separate hypothetical equity rescue includes 3%fees, integer shares and distinct pre-entry versus post-entry dilution; rescued baseIRR≈10.50% is not an ordinary target or recommendation. Rescue hurdle diagnostics at 12/15/18% are shown separately. Linked customer-loss/margin/working-capital/capex/refinancing stress tests financing, not merely terminal multiple. No DCF is forced on unreliable operating-cash/project inputs. No operational-property add-on, free IPO cash assumption, negative-cash debt fiction or post-terminal funding gap drives the five-year conclusion.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The decisive variable is conversion of concentrated reported sales into repeatable collected cash without continual new capital. One H 1 customer at 65.12% can create nonlinear effects: slower orders reduce utilization, competing suppliers compress margin, existing inventory ages, receivables stretch and bank availability tightens just as equipment payments fall due. Our linked stress uses revenue 25% below the base path, margin 3 percentage points lower, working-capital ratio 5 points higher, capex 25% higher, a 25%cash-credit call, exit multiple 3 turns lower and rescue issue price 25% lower. These are stress assumptions, not events or allegations. Positive counterevidence is substantial actual FY 26 operating earnings, receivable reduction, new IPO equity and an auditor reporting no loan default. The research hold is therefore not a claim of imminent bankruptcy. The asymmetric failure mode is that headline booked profits and stated capacity keep rising while cash and bank reconciliation do not improve, causing dilution, growth interruption or loss at a lower multiple. A documented false balance or material unreconciled cash deficit would be a thesis break; normal daily price volatility would not.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: A five-year 5× stock outcome requires 37.97% annual price growth; 10× requires 58.49%. These are stock returns, not revenue forecasts. At a 12× exit operating-EBITDA multiple and 14.5%margin, holding current shares constant and allowing no excess cash, a 5× outcome requires about₹2,949 cr revenue and 10× about₹5,877 cr, versus FY 26₹309.74 cr. Those require a demanding FY 26-to-FY 32 operating trajectory over six fiscal intervals, distinct from the five-year investor holding period; any post-entry dilution raises required aggregate equity value further. At 8× exit multiple the revenue hurdle is still larger. The claimed path to₹1,000 cr+ sales in several years does not itself deliver 5× or 10× per share from today’s capitalization. Market share, qualified customer expansion, inventory funding and proven returns on added capacity are missing links. The long-range outcome is Speculative / unsupported, not assigned a precise probability or presented as a promised target.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Review the next statutory half-year/full-year cash-flow filing, each IPO-monitoring report and material exchange filings; this is a research checklist, not a scheduled reminder. Priority 1: bank/GST reconciliation from the Q 3₹22.9937 cr bank-debtor gap baseline, with corrected signed returns and bank acknowledgment required; recurrence or material unsupported balances is a thesis-break alert. Priority 2: FY 26 CFO−₹34.77 cr, inventory₹85.08 cr and aged debtors₹3.74 cr: seek collected-cash evidence and inventory/customer rollforward, not only sales growth. Priority 3: object-wise IPOremaining₹44.80 cr atJune and capexused₹1.21 cr: require invoices, commissioning, approvals and attributable margin/cash. Priority 4: funding cash/FD/pledge reconciliation and committed limits before any ordinary valuation; a sanctioned but unavailable line is not cash. Priority 5: largest H 1 customer 65.12% and supplier 61.32%: verify current exposure and contracted replacement demand. Priority 6: test FY 27₹450–500 cr aspiration against audited margins and cash, not annualized Q 1. Priority 7: CFO transition controls and full RPT/ownership/pledge disclosures. Priority 8: verify official lot/series restrictions and daily volumes immediately before any execution assessment. Quantitative thresholds and expected documentary evidence are stored in the monitoring register.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Final classification: Hold — unresolved; research priority is reconciliation and funding verification, not eligible investment consideration or an evidence-backed compounder. All three composite scores remainNS and are excluded from point rankings. G2/G3 holds take precedence over any attractive algebraic bull-case outcome. A lower price would reduce required future operating success but cannot repair unreliable balances, unknown capital accessibility or missing attributable returns. To reopen an ordinary investment case, require a consistent financial bridge, object/pledge/bank reconciliation, credible stress financeability, project-level production/earnings/cash contribution and verified SME tradability. If those arrive, recompute factors once using the same weights, then test an ordinary base return against 15%; do not simply adopt a rescued scenario price. For an existing holding, this is a data/funding/concentration review flag, not an instruction to sell a fixed number of shares. Portfolio weights, tax consequences and live execution constraints are not known, and no trade is authorized by this research.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary evidence includes issuer annual/prospectus/operating/order/CFO filings, CRISIL monitoring and official security identity; some issuer documents were obtained through BSE-filing or broker mirrors because direct issuer links were unavailable. Document digests, original URLs, publication dates and page locators are retained. Secondary market history is explicitly segregated and filtered at 19 October; it cannot independently certify BSE execution. Latest September ownership/encumbrance, complete current RPT detail, funded cash restrictions, customer-level collections, GST/bank corrections, full FY 25-to-FY 26 restatement/CFO bridge and attributable new-capacity economics remain open. FY 22 is a short scanned startup period with no cash-flow statement found; audited full yearsFY 23–26 and H 1 FY 26 are retained without invented history. Forecast growth, margins,20%cash tax,9.75%debt interest,2%operating-cash floor, maintenance/growth capex, refinancing and terminal multiples are analyst assumptions, not management or bank commitments. Historical originals are not redistributed: analytical backups contain financial extracts, calculations, source links/hashes and reproducible code, not PDFs, OCR, images or source authentication. Calculation reproduction does not replace reobtaining and validating original disclosures.

evidence.claim: IPO6171000shares at₹149 gross₹91.9479cr. March capex/WC/GCP remaining₹24.7851/17.7668/6.8893cr; June remaining₹24.4966/13.4127/6.8893cr. Only₹1.2101cr cumulative capex used byJune.

assumptions_global.funding: Pockets are already-owned IPO money with conditional eligible releases, never new financing. No duplicate IPO proceeds or operational property add-on. Timing within phases not verified; phase-end solvency is necessary not sufficient.
assumptions_global.liability_perimeter: Legacy taxes, interest and capital creditors paid once inFY27. Gratuity retained once in terminal. Deferred tax not immediately paid again; ongoing normalized cash taxes20%.
